The exact last-shear dual and an actual boundary of the sufficient calibration
ROOT, 11 November 2026 Brisbane

Use the accepted actual determinant-one Lipschitz affine-periodic base map
f_3=id+psi from the current return, with M=Df_3. Its last vertical shear has
p(x)=r'(x), integral p=0. After the actual measure-preserving source change,
the conditional Q_0 gap is
 E+integral q_x(p(x)) dx,
 q_x(p)=B(x)p+c(x)p^2+b(x)p^3+a(x)p^4,
 a=<v^2>/96, b=<vw>/24,
 c=<6w^2+2(3v+1)^2>/96, B=<w(u+9v+6)>/24,
 u=|Me_1|^2,v=|Me_2|^2,w=Me_1.Me_2.
Here <.> is the y-average. No arbitrary matrix measure replaces M.

1. THE PAID COERCIVITY IS STRONGER THAN A BARE QUARTIC BOUND

The accepted slice identity gives <v>>=1 and <v^2>>=1. Cauchy--Schwarz gives
 a>=1/96,
 c-3b^2/(8a)>=<(3v+1)^2>/48>=1/3.
Consequently
 q_x''(p)=12a p^2+6bp+2c
         =12a(p+b/(4a))^2+2c-3b^2/(4a)>=2/3.             (1)
Thus q_x is uniformly strongly convex for EVERY actual base, independently
of any sufficient comparison of E with Var(B). B,a,b,c are bounded measurable
functions because the base is Lipschitz. This does not imply E>=0.

2. THE EXACT CONSTRAINED MINIMUM HAS A ONE-SCALAR DUAL

For each real lambda there is a unique real root p_lambda(x) of
 4a(x)p^3+3b(x)p^2+2c(x)p+B(x)+lambda=0.                  (2)
It is measurable. By (1),
 |p_lambda-p_mu|<=3|lambda-mu|/2.
The map lambda -> integral p_lambda is continuous and strictly decreasing.
At lambda=-ess sup B every root is nonnegative, while at lambda=-ess inf B
every root is nonpositive. Hence a unique lambda_* in that closed interval
satisfies integral p_lambda_*=0; the constant-B case has the same conclusion.
Also |p_lambda_*|<=3 osc(B)/2. There is no unbounded last-shear minimizer.

Let q_x^*(z)=sup_p[zp-q_x(p)]. Then
 min_(integral p=0) integral q_x(p) dx
    =sup_lambda[-integral q_x^*(-lambda) dx]
    =-integral q_x^*(-lambda_*) dx.                     (3)
Indeed the minimizing property of (2) proves the lower bound pointwise; the
bounded mean-zero p_lambda_* attains equality. Its periodic primitive r_* is
in W^(1,infinity), so the exact optimizer is an ACTUAL allowed shear. Thus
 E>=integral q_x^*(-lambda_*) dx                         (4)
is necessary AND sufficient for the original lower-endpoint conditional
last-shear Q_0 family to be nonnegative. The return's E>=3 Var(B)/4 is only
a sufficient, potentially lossy way to establish (4). A
